precepts.text: As for me, I will behold thy face in righteousness: I shall be satisfied, when I awake, with thy likeness. His likeness is righteousness. Man after his image was meant to be righteous.
precepts.point: A lot of times people think the image and likeness is only about looking like God. We know from the scriptures and history that Christ and the apostles were of our people; but being after his image is more than the hue of your skin. Black and wicked is not the way to go; there are black devils too. It is the laws of God that make us special, not color alone.

note.label: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

precepts.why:
Genesis says “after our likeness”, and Psalms 17:15 shows what that likeness is: “As for me, I will behold thy face in righteousness: I shall be satisfied, when I awake, with thy likeness.”

His likeness is righteousness. David beholds God's face in righteousness and is satisfied to wake in his likeness. So man made after God's image and likeness was meant to be righteous.

Read with Ephesians 4:24, the new man “created in righteousness and true holiness”, it is plain: black is black, but being made in his image means being black and righteous, because black and wicked ain't the way to go: you're still the devil. We say the white man's a devil, but there's black devils too. Just because you are black don't make you special unless you are righteous; it is the laws of God that make us special. The dust of the ground made the body; keeping the commandments is what makes us his likeness.

precepts.text: As for me, I will behold thy face in righteousness: I shall be satisfied, when I awake, with thy likeness. His likeness is not just appearance; it is being righteous. And in being righteous we will subdue and have dominion. That government cannot happen unless we are righteous.
precepts.point: And God said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion. Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it. Being made after his image, we were supposed to subdue the earth and bring everything underfoot. At that time everybody was of color, but God gave a specific people rulership; so when you read likeness, understand it is more than what you look like.

note.label: The Negro Community: A Wasteland of Tears

precepts.why:
Men, we want dominion. We want rulership; we want to subdue the nations. God said, “Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion,” and he told them, “Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it.” Being made after his image, we were supposed to subdue the earth and bring everything under foot.

When you read “after our likeness,” understand it is more than what you look like. At that time everybody was of color, yet God gave a specific people rulership. David shows what the likeness is: “As for me, I will behold thy face in righteousness: I shall be satisfied, when I awake, with thy likeness.”

His likeness is not just appearance; it is being righteous. Christ is black, God is black, and we are made after his image, but the image alone does not bring the dominion. In being righteous we will subdue and have dominion over things.

So the government must be in place, and in that we must be keeping the commandments. It is the only way we are going to get it. That government cannot happen unless we are righteous.

precepts.text: Deliver my soul from the wicked, which is thy sword, from men which are thy hand: the white man is the sword of the Lord.
precepts.point: O thou sword of the Lord, how long ere thou be quiet: the wicked are his sword, men which are his hand, and it cannot be quiet because the Lord has given it a charge against Ashkelon and the seashore; there hath he appointed it.

note.label: Zionism in the Face of Syria & Hezbollah

precepts.why:
Jeremiah cries, “O thou sword of the Lord, how long will it be ere thou be quiet?” What is the sword of the Lord? David shows it: “Arise, O Lord, disappoint him, cast him down: deliver my soul from the wicked, which is thy sword: From men which are thy hand, O Lord, from men of the world, which have their portion in this life, and whose belly thou fillest with thy hid treasure”.

The wicked are God's sword, men which are his hand. The white man is the sword of the Lord.

So when Jeremiah asks the sword to “put up thyself into thy scabbard, rest, and be still”, watch the response: “How can it be quiet, seeing the Lord hath given it a charge against Ashkelon, and against the sea shore? there hath he appointed it.” The Lord appointed destruction in those lands: Gaza, and Ashkelon just above it where the Israelis are, and the seashore. Baldness is come upon Gaza, and Ashkelon is cut off with the remnant of their valley, while the Muslims there cut themselves in prayer to their god, the tatbir.

The day is come “to spoil all the Philistines”, Palestine, and to cut off from Tyrus and Zidon, Lebanon, every helper that remaineth: every group they designate a terror group, like Hezbollah, which was created in 1982 to fight the Israeli invasion of Lebanon. The sword cannot be quiet, because God is causing these wars to repay the nations for what they have done to us, his chosen, Israel.

precepts.text: Arise, O Lord, disappoint him, cast him down; deliver my soul from the wicked, which is thy sword. God wields the wicked as his sword, and the wicked today is the United States. We do not bug out over what we see; we understand why it is happening and what we have to do.
precepts.point: They send drones that cost fifteen to twenty thousand dollars and the other side fires interceptors that cost a million or more to knock them down. You see how they will not be able to keep up, and how God put all this in these leaders.

note.label: Wars Are Here: Seek Good Not Evil

precepts.why:
Amos says, “And though they go into captivity before their enemies, thence will I command the sword, and it shall slay them”. Who is the sword? The wicked at the time. David shows it: “Arise, O Lord, disappoint him, cast him down: deliver my soul from the wicked, which is thy sword”, and he goes on, “From men which are thy hand, O Lord”.

God wields the wicked as his sword. The wicked today is the United States. He is going to use them to bring in all these wars you are seeing, and we have to get right.

That is why we can't bug out or get caught up in everything going on. Nobody wants to see Arab children losing limbs; nobody wants to see destruction. But we understand why it is happening, and we understand what we have to do, so that when the final war comes, he that endureth to the end shall be saved. That is what we want: deliverance.

So it was with us. The twelve tribes went into captivity after captivity before our enemies, because God allowed every bit of it. He commanded the sword and it slew us, and he set his eyes upon us “for evil, and not for good”, because we did not keep the commandments. The Iranians don't get a pass; they had us in captivity too, as did the princes of Ishmael. There is slavery happening right now in parts of Africa, and it is not Black Americans or Israelites running it, but Arabs and Caucasians with financial power. Wars are here: seek good and not evil.

precepts.text: Deliver my soul from the wicked, which is thy sword.
precepts.point: Moab shall be destroyed from being a people because he magnified himself against the Lord, and Rabbah of the Ammonites shall be a desolate heap.

note.label: Donald Trump: the Sword of God

precepts.why:
“O thou sword of the Lord, how long will it be ere thou be quiet? put up thyself into thy scabbard, rest, and be still.” A scabbard is the leather sheath you put a sword in. How long will judgment be quiet? “How can it be quiet, seeing the Lord hath given it a charge against Ashkelon, and against the sea shore? there hath he appointed it.” The seashore is Gaza. The Lord gave the sword a charge, so judgment has to go forth, and missiles are coming there too.

Who is that sword? David tells us: “Arise, O Lord, disappoint him, cast him down: deliver my soul from the wicked, which is thy sword.” The wicked is the sword of the Lord. That is why this class is called Donald Trump: the Sword of God. The Lord uses the wicked to bring judgment on the nations.

And it is judgment on all the nations, not just Esau. “Moab shall be destroyed from being a people, because he hath magnified himself against the Lord.” Concerning the Ammonites, Ammon, the Japanese: “Hath Israel no sons? hath he no heir? why then doth their king inherit Gad, and his people dwell in his cities?” Gad is mixed among them. So “I will cause an alarm of war to be heard in Rabbah of the Ammonites; and it shall be a desolate heap”, and “then shall Israel be heir unto them that were his heirs.”

Then Babylon, which is America, and the land of the Chaldeans, Amalek, the so-called Israel: “Put yourselves in array against Babylon”, “spare no arrows”, “for it is the vengeance of the Lord.” Joel says, “Prepare war, wake up the mighty men”: China, America, Russia, Iran, all must go to war and come up to the valley of Jehoshaphat, where the Lord will sit to judge all the heathen round about.

When the sword has done its work, the land comes back to us: “And the coast shall be for the remnant of the house of Judah”, and “the Lord their God shall visit them, and turn away their captivity.” The house of Judah will live in Gaza. And when Babylon falls in one hour, we are told, “Rejoice over her”, “for God hath avenged you on her.”

precepts.text: Deliver my soul from the wicked, which is thy sword.
precepts.point: The Most High ruleth in the kingdom of men and setteth up over it the basest of men. God allows what Trump is doing.

note.label: America Hedgemony & Oppression

precepts.why:
Why is God allowing Trump to do what he is doing? David answers it: “Arise, O Lord, disappoint him, cast him down: deliver my soul from the wicked, which is thy sword”. The wicked is God's sword. The so-called white man is God's sword.

So when the Most High sets up “the basest of men” over the kingdom of men, he is taking up his sword. The wicked are not ruling on their own power; they are the weapon in God's hand, the same way the king's heart is in the hand of the Lord.

And the prayer shows what the righteous do while that sword is out: cry to the Lord to deliver our souls from the wicked. The sword is being used for judgment on the earth, and only the Lord can deliver his people from it.

precepts.text: He that offends not in word is a perfect man, able to bridle the whole body; read this chapter if you struggle with a foul mouth or talking back.
precepts.point: The Most High has proved and visited him and found nothing; David is purposed that his mouth shall not transgress.

note.label: Psalm 17: Keep Me as the Apple of the Eye

precepts.why:
“I am purposed that my mouth shall not transgress.” “For in many things we offend all. If any man offend not in word, the same is a perfect man, and able also to bridle the whole body.” He that offends not in word is a perfect man, able to bridle the whole body. David prays from real and not fake lips, a prayer “that goeth not out of feigned lips”, feigned meaning fake, and he is purposed that his mouth shall not transgress.

If you struggle with a foul mouth or talking back, read this chapter of James.

precepts.text: His feet were almost gone when he was envious at the foolish and saw the prosperity of the wicked.
precepts.point: He asks the Most High to hold up his goings in his paths so that his footsteps slip not. Our footsteps slip when we come off the path of righteousness, turning to the right hand or the left instead of following the good path that leads to the kingdom.

note.label: Psalm 17: Keep Me as the Apple of the Eye

precepts.why:
David asks the Most High to “Hold up my goings in thy paths, that my footsteps slip not.” Here he shows what it looks like when the feet start to slip: “But as for me, my feet were almost gone; my steps had well nigh slipped.”

And he tells why: “For I was envious at the foolish, when I saw the prosperity of the wicked.” Envy at the foolish, looking at the prosperity of the wicked, is what nearly took his feet out from under him.

Our footsteps slip when we come off the path of righteousness, turning to the right hand or the left instead of following the good path that leads to the kingdom. Envy at the wicked is one of the things that pulls us off that path.

precepts.text: Envy not the oppressor and choose none of his ways; envy is one thing that makes the feet slip, like sticking a Christmas tree in your house and following the ways of the wicked.
precepts.point: He asks the Most High to hold up his goings in his paths so that his footsteps slip not. Our footsteps slip when we come off the path of righteousness, turning to the right hand or the left instead of following the good path that leads to the kingdom.

note.label: Psalm 17: Keep Me as the Apple of the Eye

precepts.why:
“Envy thou not the oppressor, and choose none of his ways.” Envy is one thing that makes the feet slip, and it goes together with choosing the oppressor's ways.

It is like sticking a Christmas tree in your house: envying the oppressor and following the ways of the wicked. That is coming off the path of righteousness, the very thing David prays against when he asks the Most High to hold up his goings so that his footsteps slip not.

precepts.text: Not until he went into the sanctuary of the Most High did he understand their end; get knowledge and understanding built up first.
precepts.point: He asks the Most High to hold up his goings in his paths so that his footsteps slip not. Our footsteps slip when we come off the path of righteousness, turning to the right hand or the left instead of following the good path that leads to the kingdom.

note.label: Psalm 17: Keep Me as the Apple of the Eye

precepts.why:
David's feet were almost gone when he envied the wicked, and he tells what turned it: “Until I went into the sanctuary of God; then understood I their end.” Not until he went into the sanctuary of the Most High did he understand where the wicked and their prosperity end up.

That is how the Most High holds up our goings in his paths: get knowledge and understanding built up first. With understanding of their end, the prosperity of the wicked no longer pulls the feet off the path.

precepts.text: Edom, the so-called white man or red man, says they will build the desolate places, but the Most High calls them the border of wickedness, the people against whom he has indignation forever.
precepts.point: Keep me as the apple of the eye, hide me under the shadow of thy wings. This prayer asks to be kept safe from the wicked that oppress him and from his deadly enemies who compass him about.

note.label: Psalm 17: Keep Me as the Apple of the Eye

precepts.why:
David prays to be kept “From the wicked that oppress me, from my deadly enemies, who compass me about.” Malachi names that wicked oppressor: Edom, the so-called white man or red man.

“Whereas Edom saith, We are impoverished, but we will return and build the desolate places; thus saith the Lord of hosts, They shall build, but I will throw down”. Edom says they will build the desolate places, but the Most High says he will throw it down.

And he gives them their name: “they shall call them, The border of wickedness, and, The people against whom the Lord hath indignation for ever.” Edom is the border of wickedness, the people the Most High has indignation against forever. That is the wicked David asks to be hidden from under the shadow of the Most High's wings.

precepts.text: Esau came out red all over, which identifies Edom.
precepts.point: Keep me as the apple of the eye, hide me under the shadow of thy wings. This prayer asks to be kept safe from the wicked that oppress him and from his deadly enemies who compass him about.

note.label: Psalm 17: Keep Me as the Apple of the Eye

precepts.why:
To know who Edom is, go back to the birth: “And the first came out red, all over like an hairy garment; and they called his name Esau.” Esau came out red all over, and that identifies Edom, the so-called white man or red man.

So the wicked that oppress David, his deadly enemies who compass him about, and the border of wickedness in Malachi 1:4, are the children of Esau, the one who came out red.

precepts.text: The earth is given into the hand of the wicked; the example of that wicked ruler right now is the so-called white man, not the African or the Arab.
precepts.point: Keep me as the apple of the eye, hide me under the shadow of thy wings. This prayer asks to be kept safe from the wicked that oppress him and from his deadly enemies who compass him about.

note.label: Psalm 17: Keep Me as the Apple of the Eye

precepts.why:
“The earth is given into the hand of the wicked: he covereth the faces of the judges thereof; if not, where, and who is he?” The earth is given into the hand of the wicked, and Job asks, if not, then where is he and who is he?

The example of that wicked ruler right now is the so-called white man, not the African or the Arab. He is Edom, the border of wickedness of Malachi 1:4, the red one of Genesis 25:25, and the wicked oppressor of Psalms 17:9 that David prays to be kept from as the apple of the eye, under the shadow of the Most High's wings.

precepts.text: If we keep his statutes and commandments he will give peace in the land, rid evil beasts, and the sword shall not go through our land; keeping the law is how the sword turns.
precepts.point: Arise, O Lord, disappoint him, cast him down, deliver my soul from the wicked which is thy sword. The wicked here is the same deadly enemy and oppressor named in verse 9.

note.label: Psalm 17: Keep Me as the Apple of the Eye

precepts.why:
David cries, “deliver my soul from the wicked, which is thy sword”. The wicked is the same deadly enemy and oppressor named in verse 9, and he is the Most High's sword. Leviticus shows how that sword turns.

“If ye walk in my statutes, and keep my commandments, and do them; Then I will give you rain in due season, and the land shall yield her increase”. Keep his statutes and commandments and we eat our bread to the full and dwell in our land safely. “And I will give peace in the land, and ye shall lie down, and none shall make you afraid: and I will rid evil beasts out of the land, neither shall the sword go through your land.”

Then the sword changes hands: “And ye shall chase your enemies, and they shall fall before you by the sword.” Keeping the law is how the sword turns from being upon us to falling on our enemies. That is the deliverance David asks for from men of the world which have their portion in this life, and it runs with what Bishop taught in the Sabbath class going through Job 20.

precepts.text: Esau is the wicked, the sword of the Most High, the hand of the men of the world that devours His people.
precepts.point: "But if ye refuse and rebel, ye shall be devoured with the sword." That is Israel's condition today, devoured with the sword. The sword is Esau, the wicked, whom the Most High uses to devour His people.

note.label: Isaiah 1: A Sinful Nation, Yet Zion Redeemed With Judgment

precepts.why:
“But if ye refuse and rebel, ye shall be devoured with the sword: for the mouth of the Lord hath spoken it.” That is Israel’s condition today, devoured with the sword. David shows who the sword is: “deliver my soul from the wicked, which is thy sword: From men which are thy hand, O Lord, from men of the world, which have their portion in this life, and whose belly thou fillest with thy hid treasure: they are full of children, and leave the rest of their substance to their babes.”

The sword is Esau, the wicked, whom the Most High uses to devour His people. Esau is the hand of the men of the world, who have their portion in this life. Israel refused and rebelled, so the Most High put that sword upon them.

The other side is “If ye be willing and obedient, ye shall eat the good of the land”. Eating the good of the land is not a fine restaurant; it is rulership, owning the land and the acreage free of taxes, while the other nations are put in subjection to Israel. Washing and making clean is keeping the commandments, which is how a man ceases to do evil, since evil is sin. In truth it is keep the laws or perish, yet the Most High still says “Come now, and let us reason together”: that is His mercy and love, for He has not destroyed them though He could.

precepts.text: The wicked is called the Most High's sword, showing the other nations are the weapon He uses to judge His people.
precepts.point: Gird with sackcloth, lament, and howl, for the fierce anger of the Most High is not turned back; He established it and it is going to happen.

note.label: Jeremiah 4: Return unto Me, or Destruction from the North

precepts.why:
The lion is come up from his thicket and the destroyer of the gentiles is on his way to make the land desolate; the fierce anger of the Lord is not turned back from us. David tells what that destroyer is: “Arise, O Lord, disappoint him, cast him down: deliver my soul from the wicked, which is thy sword”.

The wicked is called the Most High's sword. The other nations are the weapon he uses to judge his people. That is why the lion coming up to lay the cities waste without an inhabitant is the Lord's fierce anger and not merely an enemy's; he established it and it is going to happen, and it is why we are not in our own land today.

points: Arise, O Lord, disappoint him, cast him down: deliver my soul from the wicked, which is thy sword. So the wicked is God's sword. Who is the wicked? Esau, Edom, white supremacy. They are the oppressing sword that is going to rise up against our people. That is why the scripture says in our affliction we shall seek God early.
